Done. Solution written to **`/workspace/solution.md`**.

## What I found

I couldn't find a source repo (only `/workspace/problem.json`), so I built a faithful minimal reproduction and verified against it in genuine fresh clones.

**Root cause:** The README's source-checkout block ran `source .venv/bin/activate` on a clone where `.venv/` doesn't exist (it's `.gitignore`d). `source` fails with `No such file or directory`, but a non-`set -e` shell continues, so `pip` falls through to the system Python and hits the unrelated PEP 668 `externally-managed-environment` error.

**Critical gotcha surfaced by verification:** the obvious fix — just adding `uv venv` — is *still broken on modern uv*. `uv venv` does not seed `pip`, so after activation `which pip` is `/usr/bin/pip` and PEP 668 fires again. The corrected block must use `uv venv --seed` (or `uv pip install`).

## The fix

```bash
git clone <repo>
cd <repo>
uv venv --seed          # create .venv (with pip) before activating it
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

…plus a link to `CONTRIBUTING.md`. The pip-free variant `uv venv` + `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"` is also verified.

## Verification (fresh clones, observed)

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Original README | ❌ `No such file or directory` → PEP 668, exit 1 |
| Naive fix (`uv venv` + `pip`) | ❌ venv has no `pip` → PEP 668 |
| Recommended (`uv venv --seed` + `pip`) | ✅ install + `pytest` 1 passed |
| Alternative (`uv venv` + `uv pip`) | ✅ install + import + `pytest` pass |

The doc also includes a one-line CI regression guard and a portable checklist. I also confirmed the guard flags the broken README and passes the fixed one.
